findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a validation that exercises the metric path itself — e.g. a test/assertion that a memory datapoint survives the probe's truncation window (2684 behaviour) and that the merged run-up alarm's threshold/period actually evaluates over the 20-minute pre-collapse window — not only that the runbook names these paths.

'document why the already-merged memory alarms in monitoring_membound.tf satisfy the alarm ACs without a Terraform diff'

AC3 'An alarm fires on the RUN-UP ... not only on the aftermath'
findings.finding: AC1 (memory series survives truncation to CloudWatch) and AC3 (alarm fires on the run-up) are verified only by a pytest asserting the runbook TEXT names these paths and by an offer to 'document why the already-merged memory alarms satisfy the alarm ACs without a Terraform diff' — no test exercises the actual metric-publish path surviving the probe's SIGTERM truncation, and no test demonstrates the alarm actually fires on a simulated run-up series. Proving a runbook names a survival path is not proving the telemetry survives or the alarm fires.
findings.suggested_fix: For AC3, add an assertion over monitoring_membound.tf that the alarm's metric/period/evaluation_periods form a sustained run-up detector (not aftermath), and for AC1 add a test that the memory series datapoint density survives 2684's truncation fix over a 20-min window.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Declare AC1's dependency on change 2684 explicitly (dependency edge or merge precondition), and state the fallback (independent publisher) to keep AC1 in-session completable if 2684 has not landed.
evidence: 'Change 2684 (... currently Verified +1) is therefore ... the prerequisite for diagnosing this class of incident at all.'
AC1: 'State whether this rides on 2684's fix or needs an independent publisher, and justify.'
'Verified +1' is a pre-merge state; a prerequisite that is not merged blocks in-session completion.
findings.finding: AC1 says the memory series 'should exist' and points at change 2684 as 'the prerequisite', but 2684 is 'currently Verified +1' (not merged). If AC1 rides on 2684's fix, AC1 is not completable in-session until 2684 lands, and the plan does not declare a dependency edge or a fallback if 2684 is not merged this session.
scenarios: Executor decides AC1 rides on 2684, but 2684 is not yet merged this session — AC1 cannot be closed and the plan has no stated fallback.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a decision default: 'If 2684 is not merged this session, implement an independent memory publisher on a separate schedule so AC1 does not block on 2684.'

findings.finding: AC3 requires an alarm on 'sustained memory above a threshold' but no threshold value or sustain-duration is stated in the plan; the threshold is asserted-not-derived. findings.suggested_fix: Record the concrete alarm config (e.g. mem_used_percent > 90% for 3 of 4 consecutive 5-min periods) and show it would have triggered given the pre-incident memory trajectory.

findings.finding: The plan treats change 2684 as delivering a memory series reliable enough to show a 20-minute run-up, but this capability is not resolved: monitoring_membound.tf measured only 14-27% coverage for mem_available_percent before the fix, the alarm design conditions its own detection value on 2684 restoring coverage to >=80%, and the ignitable-fuchsia-kawala ticket records that tail metrics were still publishing zero at one point after initial landing before later verification. The plan asserts the run-up series 'should exist' post-2684 without citing the coverage evidence that would confirm it.
scenarios: Plan is accepted on the assumption 2684 already yields a run-up-grade memory series, but coverage is still below the >=80% the alarm design requires, so AC1 cannot actually be met
findings.suggested_fix: Add to AC1 a concrete coverage acceptance measured via `get-metric-statistics --period 300 --statistics SampleCount`, referencing monitoring_membound.tf's >=80% re-tune gate and the 2026-09-07 verification window so the run-up-series claim is grounded in data.
